chapter_title: Concerning the Interpretation of the Five Words th

fills.notes: The syntax requires a plural subject for “call it by this name”; the impersonal cosmological register typically uses “they” for the tradition’s speakers/knowers.

The clause “whom no one ___ his name” is a fixed apophatic formula in this substrate: the First Principle is unnameable and unknowable; “knows” fits both grammar and correspondential sense (name = quality/essence).

This is a standard triadic listing: after the Father (First) comes the Second term, here identified as the “Third Ambassador” in Manichaean/Coptic transmission. Restoring the phrase yields a coherent heading: “The second word is the Third Ambassador …”.

“Third Ambassador … of life” in this tradition generates/establishes the living structure (axis/Tree of Life) by which powers are ordered. “Father of the tree of life” is the most constrained completion before the following ellipsis.

The next phrase must link this hypostasis back to the First Father by order (discrete degrees): the Third Ambassador proceeds “after” the First Father while still being ‘of life’. This restores the missing relational clause without importing later devotional language.

To avoid a personal/filial preaching tone (“son of”), the oldest substrate typically expresses procession as rank/order. “in the order of the first Father” preserves the correspondential structure: second term derived according to the First’s degree.

assessment: ¶2 is tightly constrained by the apophatic formula about the unnameable Father and restores securely. ¶3 preserves a recognizable triadic cosmological enumeration (Father → Third Ambassador as second term), but the internal appositions (“father of …”) are only moderately constrained; restorations there are guided by standard correspondential functions (life as ordered structure/axis) and by keeping the impersonal substrate register.
